summary: You produced a good reef-monitoring SSO concept with credible STK work. Your Introduction and mission design are strong, but orbit detail errors, an unproven Vega E baseline, a generic Conclusion and referencing flaws limit you. Fixing these will lift you to the top of each rubric band.
next_steps: In Mission Design - Orbit, correct RAAN 27.33 deg and Argument of Latitude: explain RAAN/LTAN properly and give LTAN/local time for your 600km SSO.
Strengthen your Vega E from Guiana baseline with flight status and a backup launcher/SSMS option to address schedule risk you noted.
In Conclusion and throughout, add numbered figure titles, clean table formatting, and replace bare URLs/Wikipedia with proper in-text citations and reference list.

criteria.C1: You did well in Introduction stating your Earth observation mission for coral reef and ocean monitoring, justifying one satellite for simplicity, and naming users like CSIRO and BOM with literature refs. To reach the top of Accomplished, make your operator role explicit.
criteria.C2: You did well in Mission Design - Launch/Orbit and Ground Control & Communications covering Vega E from Guiana, 600km 97.7924 deg SSO, manoeuvres, Mean Duration accesses in Image 4, and 5-yr drag-sail EOL with STK screenshots. For higher Accomplished, fix RAAN-site confusion, static Argument of Latitude, missing LTAN, and mitigate Vega E risk.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion summarises launch, orbit, ground station and benefit starting 'fully described satellite configuration...'. For Accomplished, move beyond generic summary to detailed conclusions directly synthesised from your STK results, calculations and trade-offs.
criteria.C4: Your Executive Summary 'This report outlines...' and headings make the report readable. For Accomplished, give all figures numbers/titles, format tables consistently, and fix Bibliography 'https://en.wikipedia.org...' bare URLs and banned Wikipedia use with proper citations.
